newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht strong offshore late on heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht strong offshore late on heavy demand.

text.p: The Thai baht remained strong in the offshore market as offshore players continued to sell the dollar for much-needed baht late on Wednesday, dealers said.

Dealers said the demand for baht among offshore parties was much higher today after the central bank's move to prevent baht funding through the stock market and its pledge to retain a wide two-tier spread for the baht in offshore and domestic market.

The baht was quoted at 23.800/24.000 to the dollar late in offshore market after briefly surging to its new 13-year high of 23.700/23.800 in the afternoon. The baht was traded at 24.000/24.100 in early morning.
In the domestic market, the baht was slightly stronger at 25.670/25.690 against 25.710/25.730 earlier following the U.S. unit's weakness abroad, dealers said.
A senior Bank of Thailand official said on Wednesday Thailand was working on measures to formalise its recent capital controls designed to fend off future speculative attacks on the baht.
The formalisation, when it takes place, should maintain the wide spread of the baht between the baht in the offshore and onshore markets, the official told Reuters.
The central bank on Tuesday also asked bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks from foreigners in a measure to stop speculators from raising baht.
The central bank also required non-resident investors selling Thai stocks to remit funds in foreign currencies only.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was quoted at 100/120 satangs per dollar in offshore market against 18.00/22.00 in domestic market.
The overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 12.50-13.00 percent late from 13.00-13.50 in early morning, dealers said.

"The strong demand for baht will be higher tomorrow. Most custodians would begin to borrow baht to buy the dollar (for their clients) in compliance with the central bank's new regulations," said one dealer.
